title: From the Moog DFAM to the Behringer EDGE
intro: The EDGE is Behringer’s analogue recreation of the Moog DFAM, released in 2021 in a magenta desktop case. Its guide never names the DFAM, but the voice, the 8-step sequencer and the 24-jack patchbay are the DFAM’s, control for control and jack for jack, laid out differently with the patchbay along the top.

timeline.name: Moog Mother-32
timeline.text: Moog’s first semi-modular desktop synth, the start of the family the DFAM joined.

timeline.name: Moog DFAM
timeline.text: Two VCOs, noise, a ladder filter and three decay envelopes played by an 8-step pitch and velocity sequencer: a percussion synth rather than a drum machine.

timeline.name: Behringer EDGE
timeline.text: The DFAM’s voice, sequencer and patchbay, adding a NOISE COLOR switch for white or pink noise, a CLOCK switch that takes MIDI or USB clock divided by SCALE, MIDI notes that play the voice, a poly chain of up to 16 units, a headphone jack and a power switch.

relatives.name: Moog DFAM
relatives.text: The instrument the EDGE recreates, also in the app. The differences: the DFAM has white noise only, takes a clock only at ADV / CLOCK, has no MIDI, and puts its headphones on the rear output.

relatives.name: Behringer Crave
relatives.text: Behringer’s semi-modular after the Mother-32, which the EDGE sits beside as the DFAM sits beside the Mother-32.

note: The EDGE’s guide gives an outline of its MIDI; how notes play the voice comes from owners’ reports. One owner hears less low-end roundness than on the DFAM; that is not modelled, as the two share one voice here.
